bib.title: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Volume 2, Short Papers (EACL 2017)

question: Is the output embedding (topmost weight matrix) of a neural language model a valid word embedding, and does tying it to the input embedding improve language and translation models?
hypothesis: Tying input and output embeddings (U = V) reduces perplexity and parameter count in NNLMs and NMT, because the tied matrix evolves like the output embedding and overfits less.
contributions: In word2vec skip-gram the output embedding is only slightly inferior to the input embedding
In RNN language models the output embedding outperforms the input embedding
Tied embedding evolves more like the output embedding than the input embedding of the untied model
Weight tying improves perplexity of various LMs, with or without dropout
Projection regularization (matrix P before V) for models without dropout
Weight tying in NMT cuts size to less than half without harming performance

method.summary: Weight tying (U = V = S) is applied to LSTM language models (Zaremba small and large, plus RHN), word2vec skip-gram and attention NMT (DL4MT), with a three-way tying variant for NMT. For untied small models a projection P with an L2 penalty is added before the output embedding.
method.task: word-level language modelling; embedding quality; EN-FR and EN-DE machine translation

limits: Short paper; single runs, no seeds or significance tests.
NNLM hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, init) deferred to Zaremba et al. 2014 and not restated.
LSTM and RHN era models only; PTB-scale data (dataset sizes not given).
Weight tying is argued inappropriate for word2vec; it hurts embedding quality there.
Projection regularization does not help the large dropout models.
Analysis assumes input word differs from target (i_t != o_t) for simplicity.
NMT weight tying does not improve BLEU; claims only equal performance, and EN-DE decoder WT test BLEU fell 16.79 to 16.54.
